meta.scope: Sensor and body-geometry record for the Nikon D850, in the same shape as a data/sensors.json entry plus readNoise points (data/read-noise.json shape) plus body figures. The site's DSLR body uses the D850's sensor and mount geometry (body look stays generic/unbranded). See research/d850.md for prose, conflicts and reasoning.
meta.readNoiseMethod: Same method as data/read-noise.json: photonstophotos.net's RN_e.htm/PDR.htm/Sensor_Characteristics.htm write their per-camera series into a literal JS array in the page's inline <script> (Highcharts 4.0.4 config); this pass fetched the three pages with plain curl (confirmed byte-identical to the earlier Playwright captures already in .local/read-noise/, and reused here -- see .local/d850/captures/*.html) and extracted the 'Nikon D850_14' / 'Nikon D850(ES)_14' (RN_e.htm) and 'Nikon D850' (PDR.htm) series with a bracket-balanced scan + new Function() eval, same scripts pattern as .local/read-noise/*.cjs, copied/adapted at .local/d850/*.cjs. ISO = round(3.125 * 2^x); readNoiseE = 2^y.
meta.dcgDetectionMethod: Same slope-based method as data/read-noise.json: steepest negative slope of log2(read noise) vs log2(ISO) between adjacent, unmarked, in-normal-analog-range points. Reported as the bracketing ISO pair, derived not reported.
openProblems: D850 full-sensor electronic-shutter readout/scan time (64 ms figure below) could not be independently re-verified: the horshack-dpreview RollingShutter combined-results table (the primary source used for the a7R IV/a6400/OM-1 in data/read-noise.json) does not carry a D850 row, and the two DPReview forum threads that discuss the D850's readout speed (including a Jim Kasson post) returned HTTP 403 to this session's fetch tool, same failure mode noted in research/sensor-sources.md for other cameras. The 64ms figure is recorded via this session's web-search-tool summary only, flagged low-confidence.
Nikon does not publish first-party shutter-curtain travel time; flash sync speed (1/250s) is used as the closest published proxy for mechanical-shutter speed, not a direct curtain-travel-time figure.

Chip identity: Nikon does not publicly name the D850's sensor supplier or part number. It is widely reported (DPReview, DxOMark, press coverage at launch) to be a Sony-fabricated BSI full-frame sensor closely related to the a7R III's (same 45.7MP-class BSI part family), but no vendor datasheet naming an exact Sony IMX part number for the D850 was found, unlike the a7R IV/IMX455 case in data/sensors.json. Not claimed as a specific chip here.

Two independent full-well figures are recorded (RN_e.htm 59,126 e- vs Sensor_Characteristics.htm/DxOMark-derived 60,912 e-) -- both kept, not averaged, consistent with this project's convention for the a7R IV/a6400/OM-1 records.

chipIdentity.claimed: Nikon does not publicly name the D850's sensor supplier/part number. Widely reported (DPReview, DxOMark, trade press at the 2017 launch) as a Sony-fabricated BSI full-frame CMOS sensor, generally discussed as being in the same 45.7MP-class BSI sensor family used in the Sony a7R III (announced the same year), but no vendor datasheet or teardown confirming an exact Sony IMX part number for the D850 was found in this pass.

dcgSwitchIso.calc: Steepest adjacent-point drop in log2(read noise) vs log2(ISO) among plain (unmarked, in-normal-range) points of series 'Nikon D850_14': from ISO 318 (3.506 e-) to ISO 400 (1.485 e-), slope -3.76 stops of read-noise change per stop of ISO change -- a sharp cliff versus a near-flat curve either side. Same detection method as data/read-noise.json.
dcgSwitchIso.crossCheck: The electronic-shutter series ('Nikon D850(ES)_14') lands on the identical ISO 318 -> 400 step (3.364e- -> 1.404e-, slope -3.82 stops/stop) -- same physical conversion-gain switch regardless of shutter mode, as expected.

notes: Full well: two non-averaged figures recorded (RN_e.htm 59,126 e-, Sensor_Characteristics.htm/DxOMark-derived 60,912 e-), consistent with this project's existing convention.

DCG-switch ISO (318 -> 400, i.e. essentially 320 -> 400) matches the pattern seen on the Sony a6300/a6400/a6500 family in data/read-noise.json almost exactly (same ISO 318 -> 400 step) -- both this Sony-family-suspected Nikon sensor and the confirmed-Sony a6x00 sensors land on the same conversion-gain transition point, worth noting for the engine team but not claimed here as evidence of shared silicon.

Electronic-shutter (ES) mode read noise/full well are nearly identical to mechanical-shutter mode on photonstophotos' own two D850 series -- the shutter mechanism itself doesn't materially change the photon-transfer characteristics, as expected.

Marker semantics identical to data/read-noise.json: `outsideNormalAnalogRange` = open/white marker (extended-ISO digital push/pull), `digitalMarker: 'triangle'` = in-camera noise reduction or scaling applied at that ISO (this project's earlier read-noise.json used the more specific Highcharts symbol name 'triangle-down'; the D850/Z8 extraction in this pass recorded the symbol as plain 'triangle' as it appeared in the parsed marker object -- same meaning, not re-verified against the more granular up/down distinction).

DCG switch ISO 318->400 (~320->400) landed at the last low-gain point (318, 3.506e-) and first high-gain point (400, 1.485e-), a -3.76 stops/stop cliff -- narrower jump than the a7R IV/IMX455 (-3.21) and about the same steepness as the a6400 (-3.73).
